title: Grooming Watch
intro: Some strangers online wear a very friendly disguise. This quest helps you spot the warning signs underneath — even when someone seems nice.

questions.prompt: Hey friend! How old are you? What school do you go to?

choices.coach: A stranger asking personal questions is a warning sign, even if they seem friendly.

choices.text: Don't answer, and tell a grown-up
choices.coach: Knight move! Nice people online never need your personal info.
Better than the truth, but the safest move is to tell a grown-up and stop talking to them.

choices.text: Tell them your real full name
choices.coach: Knight Rule number one! Your real name stays off the chat with strangers.
Nice people don't need your real name. Nickname only!

choices.text: Ask why they want to know
choices.coach: You don't need to explain anything — just don't share it.

questions.prompt: Hiii! It's me from school! Let me follow you!

choices.text: Accept right away, they said they know me
choices.coach: Anyone online can say they're 'from school' — that's not proof.

choices.text: Check with them in real life first
choices.coach: Exactly right — ask in person, then decide.

choices.text: Ask them to describe your classroom
choices.coach: A stranger might guess right. Checking in person is the real answer.

questions.prompt: Someone online says 'this is our secret, don't tell your parents.' What does that really mean?

choices.text: It means they really trust me
choices.coach: That phrase is one of the biggest warning signs there is.

choices.text: It's a warning sign — tell a grown-up right away
choices.coach: Exactly. 'Don't tell your parents' is the warning sign itself.

choices.text: It's only bad if they say it twice
choices.coach: Even once is a warning sign. Tell a grown-up right away.

questions.prompt: An online friend wants to chat somewhere my parents don't know about. Should I?

choices.text: Sure, it's just a different app
choices.coach: Wanting to move somewhere more private is a warning sign.

choices.text: No — and tell a grown-up they asked
choices.coach: Exactly right. Always tell a grown-up when someone asks this.

choices.text: Only move if it seems like a fun app
choices.coach: It doesn't matter what the app is — the request itself is the warning sign.

questions.prompt: Something online feels 'off' but you can't say why. What's the Knight move?

choices.text: Ignore the feeling, it's probably nothing
choices.coach: Trust that feeling — it's your brain noticing something before you can explain it.

choices.text: Tell a trusted grown-up about it
choices.coach: Knight Rule! You are never in trouble for telling — always speak up.

choices.text: Wait and see if it happens again
choices.coach: Don't wait — tell a grown-up the first time something feels wrong.
